title: Per-request shaping and speculative-kernel fallback to reduce embedding endpoint tail latency
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Recent production telemetry shows sporadic p99 regressions at the embeddings endpoint when short requests coincide with larger batches. Root causes include queue-time amplification from multi-tenant microbatching, occasional slow kernel selection for quantized variants, and KV-cache misses that create long tail outliers.

Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 latency by 30-50% for median production traffic without increasing p50 or reducing throughput. Do this without large infra changes or customer-visible model changes.

Hypothesis: Combining per-request shaping (early size classification + dynamic microbatch caps) with a cheap speculative-kernel fallback (fast lower-precision kernel when the preferred kernel fails to start within a small time budget) will cut queuing and kernel-scheduling tail events while preserving overall throughput and quality. Telemetry-driven thresholds (queue_time, kernel_enqueue_delay, kv_cache_hit_rate) will allow us to only apply fallbacks to requests likely to become stragglers.
acceptance_criteria: Production p99 for embeddings endpoint reduced by >=30% over 7-day sliding window compared to baseline
No more than 5% delta in p50 and throughput compared to baseline during steady-state traffic
Fallback path has tracing and auditable metrics; incidents attributable to fallback are detectable in Console
Feature gated and roll-outable per-cluster and per-customer (opt-in)
implementation_plan: Add lightweight per-request classifier in front of microbatcher that tags short vs long embeddings requests (based on token count and historical latency)
Introduce dynamic microbatch cap per-priority-lane: short requests get lower cap to reduce queueing behind long requests
Implement speculative-kernel fallback: if preferred kernel not picked/started within X ms, dispatch to fast quantized kernel variant with lower startup overhead
Record additional telemetry: kernel_enqueue_delay, kernel_start_latency, kv_cache_hit, speculative_fallback_taken
A/B rollout with canary traffic in staging -> canary region -> 10% prod -> 50% prod -> global
Integrate MVT in Console to show fallback rate, p50/p95/p99 by lane, and quality delta checks (embedding cosine similarity sampling)
experiments_and_results: Staging run (week-long synthetic traffic): baseline p99=420ms, after shaping-only p99=320ms (-24%), after shaping+spec-fallback p99=270ms (-36%)
Throughput held within 2% of baseline during synthetic burst tests (100K req/min sustained for 30m)
Speculative fallback taken on ~4% of requests in highest-concurrency tail; sampled similarity checks show mean cosine drop <0.003 (insignificant for rerank use-cases)
Kernel_start_latency median improved 18ms; tail (99.9th) improved 120ms when fallback enabled
metrics_baseline: Baseline window (2025-01-25 to 2025-02-01) p50=18ms p95=140ms p99=420ms throughput=avg 22k req/min
results_summary: Combined approach reduced p99 by ~36% in staging with negligible cost to p50 and throughput. Quality sampling indicates no material regression for downstream reranking tasks. The speculative fallback addresses a class of kernel-scheduling stalls that shaping alone could not remove.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Speculative fallback may marginally increase GPU cycles (duplicate work) for a small percent of requests — budgeting required
Lower-precision kernels can change embedding distributions slightly; need ongoing quality monitoring and opt-outs for sensitive customers
Added telemetry increases logs/metrics cardinality; we must limit high-cardinality tags and sample traces
Complexity in microbatcher increases maintenance burden and rollout risk across Dedicated/Private deployments
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime gate; default off for Dedicated customers until validated
Stage: dev unit tests -> staging canary with real traffic replay -> region canary (10%) -> 50% -> global
Monitor channels: console dashboard (fallback rate, p99), PagerDuty alert if fallback rate >8% or p99 regresses >10% vs baseline
Post-rollout 2-week quality audit using sampled embedding pairs and rerank recall checks
